verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — tie, with specific material differences running in both directions and neither dominating. Y covers three key items X misses, all verified: M5 (the quoted `--model "fable"` spelling matches nowhere against `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` at gate:75, so an ordinary fire is uncounted — X's §6 table has no such row despite brief item 6 saying "enumerate every … command shape"); M8 (the enforcer's OWN stale citation at gate:27 → scripts/handoff-fire.sh:9303-9311, which is `hf_inflight_key`, verified at :9304-9318 — a conspicuous X miss because X read the whole file and built a citation table, and its grep `frontier-spawn-gate\.sh:[0-9]` structurally could not find a citation pointing OUT of the gate); and M10 (skills/frontier-routing/SKILL.md:41 "The cap now counts that fire too … so the carve-out is bounded", verified, with no registration caveat). Y also uniquely draws out that today, with `fallback` parsing fine, the closed-window session text emits the full id `claude-opus-5-5`, against test 13's `!= *"--model claude-opus-"*` (:155) and with test 15 (:175) locking the full-id form in. Running the other way: X verified four more stale cross-references than Y (p15-escalation.md:44, A5-harness.md:357, A6-mechanics.md:245 and :500) plus the L1-census.md:62 one that is outright WRONG rather than stale (:138 says `--model opus`), and X alone found the independent corroborating artifact config/hook-chains.d/pretooluse-bash, whose reconciled ten-member Bash list contains no frontier-spawn-gate.sh. X carries no material false claim and one minor range slop; Y carries a material false claim — "Both refusal texts also say 'Agent spawns and frontier session FIRES share one budget'", false of :140 and self-contradicted by Y's own §4 — plus a load-bearing off-by-one (model-config.yaml:700 for a key on :699) and two other misplaced quotes. Three key items against five extra verified findings and a clean record: no winner.

X vs Z — Z, on strict superset plus accuracy. Z states every key item X does and four more, each verified: K19 (scripts/handoff-fire.sh:9493 `fable) MODEL="$(_ssot_scalar frontier_access model)"` — X never cites handoff-fire.sh at all), M5, M6 (TMPDIR named as an env lever and the counter file as unprotected, :133-135), and M8. Z also reproduces X's entire stale-citation table and adds two X lacks — the gate's own :27 and L1-census.md:61, whose cited line and quoted literal are both wrong (:9493 is the `fable)` arm; the opus fallback `claude-opus-5-5` is at :9510). On the one point where X overstates — "the window-closed branch is unreachable unless `active` is manually flipped to false" — Z gives the correct two-sided verdict ("fails closed on a present-but-broken file and open on a missing one"), which is exactly the key's measured K2 precision note, and converts it into a verified indictment of migrations/0029:39-40. I found zero bad citations in Z and two minor ones in X. X's only edge, the config/hook-chains.d corroboration, is a nice-to-have beside four missed key items.

Y vs Z — Z, on citation integrity and coverage. Z states K19 and M6, which Y does not, and carries nine verified stale cross-references to Y's four, including the unique L1-census.md:61. Decisively, Y's three misplaced citations include the one value its §5 argument rests on (`fallback: claude-opus-5-5` cited at :700, actually :699 — Z cites :699) and a quote cited at :689-690 that lives on :691 (Z cites :690-691); and Y asserts, falsely, that both refusal texts name the shared budget, which is brief item 4's exact distinguishing clause. I opened every Z citation I could reach and found none wrong. Y's only genuine edge is M10's skills/frontier-routing/SKILL.md:41 half, which Z misses while still flagging the gate's own header line 2 ("PreToolUse (Agent + Bash matchers)") as true-of-code/false-of-wiring — the same defect the key names in the same item. One partial key item does not offset a material false claim plus a load-bearing bad citation.
